model_output.summary: Your work centers on commercial furniture design, from sheet-metal parts and BIFMA prototype testing to leading mechanical design for the Arlo desk platform. Naming the platform is worth keeping because it gives the current role a concrete product. The progression from Mechanical Engineer I to II fits the move from component design to platform-level responsibility. A reviewer may still wonder which technical decisions you made on Arlo and how they affected the design.
strengths: Supplier work in Mexico and Taiwan puts tooling and first-article inspection in an international manufacturing context.
Tolerance stack-ups and FEA on load-bearing components show the kinds of analyses involved in your current work.
BIFMA prototype testing connects your earlier design work to a recognized furniture standard.
gaps: The Arlo bullet doesn't identify the parts or design decisions within your responsibility, making the lead role difficult to assess in detail.
The supplier bullet names tooling and inspection but not a specific issue you worked through with either supplier.
The testing and analysis bullets don't describe findings or changes, so their contribution to the products is unclear.
